exposure: unintended upper uterine wall extensions during cesarean delivery
outcome: unintended upper uterine wall extensions during cesarean delivery
cohort: The cohort consisted of 30,517 patients who underwent cesarean delivery between 2005 and 2021.
finding: Unintended upper uterine wall extensions during cesarean delivery are infrequent (0.4%) but are significantly associated with increased maternal and neonatal complications, with key risk factors including fetal extraction not by head, second-stage CD, and trial of labor after cesarean.
mod_finding: Unintended upper uterine wall extensions occur in 0.4% of cesarean deliveries, with second-stage CD and CD following trial of labor after cesarean identified as significant risk factors.
